observation_summary: The method NumberUtils.createNumber was incorrectly returning null when encountering a string starting with '--', instead of throwing a NumberFormatException as expected by the API contract and other validation logic.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved removing an incorrect conditional check from the main entry point (createNumber) and moving a more robust validation check (including a trim() call and throwing a proper exception) into the specific method (createBigDecimal) that actually handles the problematic input. This is a classic case of correcting validation logic (a guard) to ensure consistent API behavior.
evidence_used: The fix removes an 'if (str.startsWith("--")) { return null; }' block from createNumber.
The fix adds a 'if (str.trim().startsWith("--")) { throw new NumberFormatException(...); }' block to createBigDecimal.
The bug report states that returning null is contrary to the Javadoc and the behavior of other methods which throw NumberFormatException.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the behavior was inconsistent with the API contract, the root cause was a missing/incorrect validation check (guard) within the implementation, which is the definition of Checking.
The fix is not about the computational logic of parsing numbers, but about validating the input string before processing it.
